The '''2022–23 Premier League''' was the 31st season of the [[Premier League]] and the 124th season of top-flight English football overall. [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] were the three promoted clubs from the [[2021–22 EFL Championship]], replacing [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] and [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].

Following [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s defeat to Nottingham Forest on 20 May, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] officially secured a [[Three-peat|third consecutive]] Premier League title with three games to spare, becoming the second club after local rivals [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] to achieve the feat in the Premier League era. It was their ninth English title overall and their seventh since 1992.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3446899|title=Man City are 2022/23 champions after Arsenal defeat|publisher=Premier League|date=20 May 2023|access-date=20 May 2023}}</ref> The league title was the first leg in a [[Treble (association football)#Continental trebles|treble-winning season]] for City, as they would later go on to win the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], a feat which only United had previously achieved in England. Meanwhile, Arsenal broke the record of spending the greatest number of days, with 248, on top of the league in a top flight season without winning the title in English top flight history.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=OptaJoe |number=1659991615853699083 |title=248 - Arsenal led the Premier League table for 248 days in 2022-23, the most for a team who failed to win the title in English top-flight history. Agonising. |author=OptaJoe |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=21 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230521063409/https://twitter.com/OptaJoe/status/1659991615853699083 |url-status=live}}</ref>

This season was also the first since [[2017–18 Premier League|2017–18]], and only the fourth Premier League season overall, where all three promoted teams at the start of the season avoided relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3447125|title=Nottingham Forest secure Premier League safety|date=20 May 2023|access-date=20 May 2023}}</ref> This was also the first time since [[2014–15 Premier League|2014–15]] that the team 20th at Christmas ([[2022-23 Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. season|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]), managed to avoid relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/wolves-julen-lopetegui-premier-league-29923302.amp |title=Inside Julen Lopetegui's Wolves revival as Premier League survival officially secured|publisher=The Mirror|first=Ben|last=Husband|date=8 May 2023|access-date=30 May 2023}}</ref>

The 2022–23 season was the highest-scoring 38-game season in Premier League history, with 1,084 goals scored and a 2.85 goals per match ratio.<ref>{{cite news |title=Record set for goals in a Premier League season |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3490140 |publisher=Premier League |date=28 May 2023}}</ref> [[Erling Haaland]] broke the Premier League record for most goals scored by a player in one season with 36 goals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Haaland claims 2022/23 Golden Boot |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3486228 |publisher=Premier League |date=28 May 2023}}</ref>

It was also the second Premier League season in a row where over 15 millions fans attended matches and with total of 15,289,340 spectators a new competition record was set.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/premier-league-attendances-at-record-high-as-crowds-swell-across-the-pyramid-6nm7t8fn0 |title=Premier League attendances at record high as crowds swell across the pyramid |last=Edgar |first=Bill |date=11 April 2023 |work=[[The Times]] |access-date=11 June 2023 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Summary==
The season began with Arsenal going on a five-game unbeaten streak before they played [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]] where they lost 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12687857/manchester-united-3-1-arsenal-marcus-rashford-scores-twice-after-antony-debut-goal-ends-gunners-perfect-start |title=Manchester United 3-1 Arsenal: Marcus Rashford scores twice after Antony debut goal ends Gunners' perfect start |publisher=Sky Sports |date=5 September 2022 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] got off to a strong start, having signed striker [[Erling Haaland]]; they went on a nine-game unbeaten run before losing at [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in October. Arsenal were top of the table for much of the season, at one point holding an eight point lead over Manchester City. However, a run of three consecutive draws allowed City to cut their lead, ultimately taking control after beating them 4–1 at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]]. Two consecutive losses against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] left Arsenal four points behind Manchester City with three more games to play, with the latter result confirming City as champions.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65579920 |title=Nottingham Forest 1-0 Arsenal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> They were presented with the Premier League trophy on 21 May 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/manchester-city-lift-the-premier-league-trophy-erling-haaland-kevin-de-bruyne-pep-guardiola-get-silverware/ |title=Manchester City lift the Premier League trophy: Erling Haaland, Kevin de Bruyne, Pep Guardiola get silverware |publisher=CBS Soccer |date=21 May 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref>

Manchester United returned to the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] in [[Erik ten Hag]]'s debut season as the club's manager, in addition to winning the [[2022–23 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]] – their first trophy since [[2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season|2017]] – and reaching the [[2023 FA Cup final|final]] of the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]]. [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] qualified for the Champions League for the first time in [[2002–03 Newcastle United F.C. season|20 years]], their highest finish since [[Bobby Robson|Sir Bobby Robson]] was the club's manager.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/05/23/sport/newcastle-united-champions-league-qualification-spt-intl/index.html |title=For the first time in 20 years, Newcastle United will play in the Champions League |publisher=CNN Sports |date=23 May 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> Liverpool endured a difficult season and finished 5th, missing out on Champions League football for the first time since [[2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season|2015–16]]. Notably, they thrashed [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] [[Liverpool F.C. 9–0 AFC Bournemouth|9–0]] and rivals Manchester United 7–0.

Despite spending over £600m on new transfers under new ownership led by [[Todd Boehly]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] had one of their worst Premier League seasons to date, with the Blues finishing in the bottom half of the table after first sacking [[Thomas Tuchel]] in September, and then sacking his successor [[Graham Potter]] the following April, after only seven months in charge. [[Frank Lampard]] returned to the club as interim manager, having previously been sacked himself in January 2021, but the team fared no better under his stewardship either. They ended up finishing 12th, their lowest league finish since [[1993–94 Chelsea F.C. season|1993–94]], and had accumulated just 44 points – their lowest ever in a Premier League season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/chelsea-in-serious-danger-of-recording-worst-ever-premier-league-finish-as-winless-run-continues |title=Chelsea guaranteed to record worst-ever Premier League finish even with two games remaining |publisher=FourFourTwo |date=25 May 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref>

Brighton & Hove Albion lost manager Potter to Chelsea in September, but his successor [[Roberto De Zerbi]] led the team to a club record finish of 6th, and qualified for the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]], the first European qualification in the history of the club.<ref name="MacInnes 2023">{{cite web | last=MacInnes | first=Paul | title=Brighton seal historic European spot as Ferguson double sinks Southampton | website=the Guardian | date=21 May 2023 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/may/21/brighton-southampton-premier-league-match-report | access-date=31 May 2023}}</ref>

[[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] secured qualification for European football for the first time since [[2009–10 Aston Villa F.C. season|2009–10]]; an indifferent start to the season saw the departure of manager [[Steven Gerrard]], but his successor [[Unai Emery]], along with in-form striker [[Ollie Watkins]], saw Villa climb the table in the second half of the season to finish 7th and qualify for the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League|Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/soccer/futbol/news/aston-villa-qualify-for-europa-conference-league-tottenham-dont |title=Aston Villa qualify for european football as Tottenham miss out for first time in 14 seasons |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=28 May 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] had an erratic season, with manager [[Antonio Conte]] departing by mutual consent in March, days after publicly criticising the team in a post-match press conference.<ref>{{cite web | title=Conte press conference: My players were selfish | website=Premier League Football News, Fixtures, Scores & Results | date=18 March 2023 | url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/3115831 | access-date=31 May 2023}}</ref> He was initially replaced by his assistant [[Cristian Stellini]] until the end of the season, but a poor run, culminating in a 6–1 defeat away to Newcastle, where the team were 5–0 down after just 20 minutes, saw him sacked and replaced by [[Ryan Mason]] as caretaker manager. Tottenham ended up finishing 8th, failing to qualify for European football for the first time since [[2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2008–09]], and finishing below rivals Arsenal in the league for the first time since [[2015–16 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2015–16]].

[[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] enjoyed one of the best seasons in their history, at one point going on a 12-match unbeaten run. They notably thrashed Manchester United 4–0 and beat Liverpool 3–1, and were the only team to beat Manchester City twice. Their 9th-place finish marked their highest finish in top-flight football since 1938.

Bournemouth, who were tipped for relegation at the start of the season (particularly after their 9–0 loss to Liverpool at [[Anfield]], which saw manager [[Scott Parker]] sacked soon after),<ref>{{cite news |title=Why Bournemouth are sleepwalking towards disaster|url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2022/08/02/why-bournemouth-sleepwalking-towards-disaster/|publisher=The Telegraph|first=Jason|last=Burt|date=2 August 2022|access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref> defied the critics by avoiding relegation, with [[Gary O'Neil]], first as interim, then permanent manager, guiding the team to safety. Nottingham Forest broke the record for most signings in a Premier League season with 21,<ref>{{cite news |title=All Nottingham Forest's 21 summer signings as Premier League transfer record broken|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/nottingham-forest-premier-league-signings-27890204.amp|publisher=The Mirror|first=Kieran|last=King|date=2 September 2022|access-date=30 May 2023}}</ref> and a late run of home victories over Brighton, [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and Arsenal secured safety. The final newly promoted side, [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], enjoyed a successful return to the top flight with a 10th place finish.

Southampton were the first team to be relegated after eleven consecutive years in the top flight. The Saints sacked [[Ralph Hasenhüttl]] in November after just under four years in charge and [[Nathan Jones (Welsh footballer)|Nathan Jones]] was appointed as his successor. He would then be dismissed in February after winning just once in his eight league matches in charge. He was replaced for the rest of the season by [[Rubén Sellés]], who was unable to turn the dire situation around, and a 2–0 home loss to Fulham on 13 May sealed their fate, as they finished at the bottom of the table.

Going into the final day of the season, two relegation places were still to be confirmed, with [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] all potentially at threat of relegation. Leeds failed to repeat their last day escape of the [[2021–22 Premier League|previous season]] and were also relegated after three years back in the top flight, losing 4–1 at home to Tottenham Hotspur. Everton escaped relegation after a 1–0 win over Bournemouth, extending their top flight stay to a 70th consecutive year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230528-everton-must-start-performing-like-a-big-club-warns-dyche|title=Everton must start performing like a big club, warns Dyche|date=28 May 2023|website=France 24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/everton-vs-bournemouth-video-highlights-analysis-recap|title=Everton beat Bournemouth to save themselves from relegation|date=29 May 2023|website=NBC Sports}}</ref> The Toffees' survival confirmed Leicester's relegation after a nine year stay in the top flight, despite a 2–1 home win over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]]. Their relegation came only [[2015–16 Premier League|seven years]] after being crowned champions of England, and they became only the second club in the Premier League era after [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] to be relegated as previous title winners.<ref>{{cite news |title=Which two football clubs have suffered relegation from Premier League despite winning the title once?|url=https://firstsportz.com/football-which-two-football-clubs-have-suffered-relegation-from-premier-league-despite-winning-the-title-once/|publisher=First Sportz|first=Anany|last=Kapoor|date=29 May 2023|access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref>

===Developments===
Starting from the 2022–23 season, clubs are able to make five [[Substitute (association football)|substitutions]] rather than three. These substitutions can be made in three stoppages during game time, and additionally at half time,<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League clubs agree to five substitutes from 2022–23 season |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60945430 |date=31 March 2022 |access-date=8 June 2022 |publisher=Premier League |archive-date=8 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220608015705/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60945430 |url-status=live }}</ref> in line with other top European leagues – [[Serie A]], [[La Liga]], [[Ligue 1]] and the [[Bundesliga]].{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

There was a mid-season break for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar, with the last matches before the hiatus played on the weekend of 12–13 November 2022 and the first matches after the World Cup played on 26 December 2022, after the [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|World Cup final]] on 18 December 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League 2022/23 dates announced |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2264107 |date=11 November 2021 |access-date=14 April 2022 |publisher=Premier League |archive-date=18 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918220148/https://www.premierleague.com/news/2264107 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2021–22 EFL Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], who returned to the top flight after respective absences of one, two and twenty-three years. They replaced [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] (relegated to the [[2022–23 EFL Championship|Championship]] after a six-year top flight spell), [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], and [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] (both teams relegated after just one year back in the top flight).{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}
